title: Dispatch: clause IR review corrections from PR #475 (attempt 2)
description:
HUMAN REVIEW OF PR #475 returned "changes required": three P1 findings and one
P2. All four are accepted. Read the inline comments on
https://github.com/jbongaarts/eshyra/pull/475 for the reviewer's exact wording,
then fix the underlying design — not just the cited line.

=== FILES YOU OWN ===
  docs/adr/0020-source-clause-semantic-ir-and-completeness-contracts.md
  packages/core/src/rules/clauseIr/types.ts
  packages/core/src/rules/clauseIr/contracts.ts
  packages/core/src/rules/clauseIr/index.ts
  packages/core/test/clauseIrContracts.test.ts

=== P1-A: COMPLETENESS IS NOT SOURCE-SPECIFIC (contracts.ts:48) ===
Today the only authority is the projector-selected ClauseKind plus a generic
field list. Nothing binds an exact source clause to the semantic obligations
actually present in its source text.

The reviewer's worked example, which your tests must cover: a source clause
containing a save, a duration, a repeated save, and a termination condition can
be emitted as `kind: 'save'`. The save contract never requires duration,
repeatChecks or termination — so the evaluator CERTIFIES the partial projection.
That is the audit's root failure reproduced inside the very mechanism built to
prevent it.

Fix: completeness must be driven by SOURCE-BACKED PER-CLAUSE OBLIGATIONS, not by
the selected kind. Concretely, the clause must declare the obligations detected
in its source span, and the evaluator must require each declared obligation to
be discharged by a satisfied contract. Support composed contracts and/or child
clauses so one source clause can carry several obligations. A projector that
selects a narrower kind than its source text supports must fail closed rather
than silently narrowing.

You choose the exact representation, but the invariant is: the SOURCE decides
what must be present; the kind only decides HOW it is shaped.

=== P1-B: REQUIRED COLLECTIONS PASS WHEN EMPTY (contracts.ts:298) ===
Only `sourceSpans` has a cardinality check. Every other required array —
`saves`, `attacks`, `damage`, `alternatives`, `ledgerChanges`,
`stateTransitions`, `regressionEvidence` — passes when `[]`. A save clause
with `saves: []` and `damage: []`, populated branches and all dimensions true
returns `complete`. That directly violates the fail-closed invariant.

Fix: the contract vocabulary needs requirement PREDICATES with cardinality, not
boolean field presence. Include cross-field alternatives where the source
genuinely allows them (an attack roll XOR a saving throw, for example) so the
fix does not force absurd requirements. Add a test for the exact empty-array
case above.

=== P1-C: THE EVALUATOR COLLAPSES THE FOUR DIMENSIONS (contracts.ts:91) ===
ADR 0020 says CAPTURED, PROJECTED, SUPPORTED and DISCOVERABLE must fail
INDEPENDENTLY and no gate may collapse them. Requiring all four in every
ClauseCompletenessContract means a fully captured and projected clause that is
merely awaiting an engine or lookup path is labelled generically "incomplete".

*** THIS ONE IS MY FAULT, NOT YOURS. *** The attempt-1 dispatch spec explicitly
instructed that a CAPTURED+PROJECTED-but-not-SUPPORTED clause must not evaluate
complete, and the test at clauseIrContracts.test.ts:180-213 faithfully locks that
in. That instruction was wrong. You are expected to CHANGE that test.

The distinction to encode:
  * SEMANTIC COMPLETENESS — is the projection of this source clause complete?
    Determined by CAPTURED and PROJECTED and the source obligations from P1-A.
  * READINESS — can it execute end to end? SUPPORTED and DISCOVERABLE, reported
    per dimension.
A clause can be semantically complete and unsupported; that is the exact
distinction the audit needed and the pack lacked. Return independently gated
per-dimension results, or separate the two evaluations. Do not emit a single
all-or-nothing status that hides which dimension failed.

The nine-point green definition on eshyra-o9bd.19 still governs the FREEZE gate
and still requires an engine implementation — but that is a freeze gate, not a
clause-completeness verdict, and must not be smuggled into this evaluator.

=== P2-D: DISPOSITION CAN CONTRADICT THE CLAUSE (types.ts:277) ===
`disposition`, the dimension booleans and the free-text `note` can contradict
one another, and `evaluateClauseCompleteness` ignores `disposition` entirely.
So `disposition: 'complete'` with `projected: false` is legal, and
`disposition: 'incomplete'` with everything satisfied evaluates complete. The
clause also carries no structured failed-contract reasons, although the ADR
requires an emitted INCOMPLETE clause to NAME each failed requirement.

Fix: make the status derived/canonical, or validate consistency and fail closed
on contradiction; and carry structured contract failures on the emitted clause —
or make the evaluation result the sole authoritative readiness artifact and stop
storing a disposition that can drift.

=== ADR 0020 ===
Update it to match. It is the document the rest of the program will cite, so the
source-obligation rule, the cardinality rule, and the independence of the four
dimensions must be stated there, not only in code.

=== UNCHANGED ===
Design and type contracts only — no importer changes, no projector changes, no
pack regeneration. Small hand-built fixtures; do not load the 7.4 MB pack. No
hand-copied counts. Qualified engine:F* / fable:F* / opus:F-* / sol:CAP-* /
indep:* prefixes only, never a bare "F5".

=== ENVIRONMENT AND VERIFICATION ===
This worktree already contains the previous attempts' committed work; you are
correcting it, not starting over. Run `npm ci` FIRST. Run
`npm run verify:worktree` BEFORE committing — it rewrites files.

=== HARD CONSTRAINTS ===
* Edit ONLY the files listed under FILES YOU OWN. A sibling dispatch is running
  in parallel on a disjoint file set. Do not touch package.json,
  packages/core/package.json, or packages/core/src/internal.ts.
* Do NOT modify any bead except your own. Do NOT run `bd dolt push`.
* Do NOT push, do NOT open or comment on a PR, do NOT merge.
* Do NOT weaken, skip, or delete an existing test to make a finding go away. If
  an existing test encodes the defective behavior, CHANGE it deliberately and
  say so in your completion notes with the reason.
* Do NOT regenerate the rules pack and do NOT run the SRD importer.
acceptance_criteria:
• Completeness is driven by source-backed per-clause obligations; the reviewer's save+duration+repeat+termination example fails closed and is covered by a test.
• Required collections have cardinality/predicate requirements; the empty-saves/empty-damage case evaluates incomplete and is covered by a test.
• Semantic completeness and readiness are separated; the four dimensions report independently and no single verdict hides which failed.
• The attempt-1 test that locked in dimension collapse is deliberately changed, with the reason recorded.
• A clause cannot carry a disposition that contradicts its dimensions, and an incomplete clause structurally names its failed requirements.
• ADR 0020 states all of the above.
• npm run verify:worktree passes.
notes: Completion report (review-correction): corrected PR #475 findings across the owned ADR, clause IR types/contracts/index, and contract tests. SourceObligation now binds source text and exact source-span locators, supports composed contract kinds and source-specific predicates; contracts use cardinality predicates and field-group alternatives; evaluator returns semantic completeness separately from independent CAPTURED/PROJECTED/SUPPORTED/DISCOVERABLE readiness. Removed stored readiness disposition so it cannot contradict dimensions; evaluator returns structured source-linked failures. Deliberately changed the prior dimension-collapse test because the original dispatch instruction was wrong: CAPTURED+PROJECTED but unsupported is semantically complete yet not ready. I agree with all four review findings and disagree with none. Verification: npm ci; npm run verify:worktree passed (263 files passed, 4 skipped; 4718 tests passed, 19 skipped). Follow-up filed: eshyra-o9bd.19.1.1.2.1. No importer, pack, parent bead, push, PR, or bd dolt push touched.
